issues.description: The assembleBookstore function signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template indicate assembleBookstore should have no parameters (private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore), but the solution defines assembleBookstore(seed: Double) -> Bookstore while Client.main() calls assembleBookstore() with no arguments. This creates a parameter mismatch and a compilation/runtime inconsistency — students following the template/problem will expect a no-argument function, and the provided solution is internally inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the assembleBookstore signature consistent with the problem statement and template by removing the seed parameter in the solution: change private static func assembleBookstore(seed: Double) -> Bookstore to private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore. Alternatively, update Client.main() to call assembleBookstore with an appropriate Double argument, but aligning to the no-argument version is recommended to match the exercise description.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an assembleBookstore() function with no parameters, but the solution implements assembleBookstore(seed: Double) — the added parameter changes the function signature for the same conceptual entity (assembling the bookstore) and can confuse students when mapping the required function to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the assembleBookstore function signature consistent across artifacts. Either remove the seed parameter from the solution (change to private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore) or update the problem statement and template to require assembleBookstore(seed: Double) and document the purpose of the seed.
